summary: This bill amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to add priority consideration for certain DOJ grants to applicants from states or localities that have signed 287(g) agreements allowing local law enforcement to perform federal immigration enforcement functions.

scores.thoughts: The bill modifies grant prioritization under an existing federal grant program (Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act) but does not alter overall funding levels, authorize new appropriations, or expand/reduce government spending. It only changes which applicants receive priority consideration.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment rights.

The bill directly incentivizes state and local participation in federal immigration enforcement by giving priority grant consideration to jurisdictions that enter into 287(g) agreements under the Immigration and Nationality Act. This explicitly promotes cooperation with border enforcement and interior immigration enforcement, aligning strongly with the restrict/enforce end of the spectrum.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

While the bill amends a crime control grant statute, its sole purpose is to tie grant priority to immigration enforcement cooperation rather than addressing criminal justice reforms, sentencing, or policing practices. The connection is incidental and not substantive.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill contains no provisions related to deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or voter ID.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
The bill contains no provisions related to unions, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
